Configuration ​

FaultDeck has no config files — everything is passed as CLI flags/args at process start. Values below are the defaults from the source.

faultdeck-agent ​

flagdefaultnotes
--bind ADDR127.0.0.1:7000TCP listen address
--token TOKENunset → auth disabledwhen set, every request line must start with <token>
--interface IFACEeth0interface for the tc adapter
--management CIDRemptyrepeatable; protected networks, overlap rejects injection
--iptables PATHnonerequired for disconnect; without it the agent answers iptables missing

Behavioral constants (compiled in, not configurable):

constantvaluewhere
max request payload64 KiBfaultdeck_agent::MAX_INJECTION_BYTES
pilot qdisc handle100:faultdeck_netem::PILOT_QDISC_HANDLE
netem qdisc handle50:adapter-internal
max latency86 400 000 ms (24 h)faultdeck_core::MAX_LATENCY_MS
iptables chainFAULTDECK in table manglefaultdeck_agent::firewall::CHAIN

AgentConfig (the library struct behind the flags) also serializes to JSON, so agents can be constructed programmatically.

faultdeck-coordinator ​

bash
faultdeck-coordinator [BIND]     # default 127.0.0.1:7001

One positional argument only. State (registry, report archive, routes) is in-memory.

faultdeck (CLI) ​

flagapplies todefaultnotes
--hostall remote subcommandsrequiredagent address
--portall remote subcommands7000agent port
--tokenall remote subcommandsnoneprefixed to the request line
--faultinjectrequiredlatency | loss | disconnect
--destinationinjectrequiredIPv4 CIDR
--port-specinjectnoneoptional destination-port match
--millisecondsinject --fault latencyrequired by that faultdelay
--percentinject --fault lossrequired by that faultloss percent
--scenario-nameinject"scenario"report label
--report-jsoninjectnonewrite JSON report locally
--report-htmlinjectnonewrite HTML report locally

There are no environment variables, no config file lookup, and no daemon options beyond the flags above.
